issues.fix: Use `$Host.UI.PromptForCredential('AutoWiFi BITS', 'BITS campus ID and password', '', '')` (or bare `Get-Credential` without `-Message`), exit 0 with empty stdout when the returned credential is `$null` (user cancelled), and distinguish real PowerShell errors from user cancellation instead of mapping every `*exec.ExitError` to `ErrCancelled`.
issues.problem: `Get-Credential -Message '...'` without `-UserName` fails in Windows PowerShell 5.1 (`powershell.exe`, the default on Windows 10/11). In PowerShell 5.1, `-Message` selects the `Message` parameter set where `-UserName` is mandatory (and passing `-UserName ""` also fails parameter binding), so `powershell.exe` prompts for `UserName:` on closed stdin and exits non-zero before any dialog appears. Because lines 29-32 map every `*exec.ExitError` to `ErrCancelled`, both Windows first-run setup and tray "Set ID and password…" (the primary flow documented in `site/index.html:153`) silently fail as cancelled with no dialog and no error shown.

issues.fix: Link to `https://github.com/AdityaEvilIncorporated/automaticwifi-bits/blob/HEAD/ios/SHORTCUT_GUIDE.md` (which resolves to the repository's default branch) or `blob/dev/ios/SHORTCUT_GUIDE.md`, and verify the URL in `internal/docscheck/docs_test.go`.
issues.problem: The iPhone setup section links to `blob/main/ios/SHORTCUT_GUIDE.md`, but `dev` is the GitHub default branch and `main` is an empty commit (`git ls-tree main` has no files; `.github/workflows/pages.yml` deploys from `dev`). The published GitHub Pages link will return HTTP 404 for iOS users until `main` is manually populated.

issues.fix: Use `exec.Command("/usr/bin/launchctl", args...).CombinedOutput()` and include stderr in the returned error so `"already"` checks actually work. Also consider avoiding `launchctl bootout` terminating the running agent mid-call when triggered from the tray's "Start at login" toggle while launched by launchd.
issues.problem: `launchctl` uses `exec.Command(...).Run()`, which discards stderr and produces an `*exec.ExitError` whose `.Error()` is only `"exit status N"`. Line 39 checks `!strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(err.Error()), "already")` to ignore an already-bootstrapped LaunchAgent, which can never match. Additionally, calling `launchctl bootout gui/<uid>/<Label>` from inside a launchd-started tray agent sends SIGTERM to itself, so toggling "Start at login" off in the macOS tray kills the running tray app.

issues.fix: Loop over subsequent matches in `findPortalToken` until a non-empty `[0-9A-Za-z]+` token is found (matching `internal/portal/classify.go:274-289`), and add a shared test case in `protocol/testcases/login_reply.json`.
issues.problem: `findPortalToken` only inspects the first occurrence of `{portalBase}/{path}?` in `location` or `body`. If a login reply mentions `{portalBase}/keepalive?` without a token (e.g. in a JS template/variable) before the real `{portalBase}/keepalive?<token>`, Kotlin returns `""` and misclassifies a valid login as `form_changed` (or `rejected`), diverging from Go's `findPortalToken` in `internal/portal/classify.go:274-289`.

issues.fix: Force base-10 arithmetic: `export APP_VERSION_CODE=$(( 10#$major * 10000 + 10#$minor * 100 + 10#$patch ))` and assert `APP_VERSION_CODE -ge 1`.
issues.problem: `APP_VERSION_CODE=$(( major * 10000 + minor * 100 + patch ))` parses version components without a `10#` base prefix. A tag accepted by the line 41 regex that has a leading zero (e.g. `v0.08.0`) fails bash arithmetic as an invalid octal literal (or miscomputes octal for `010`), and `v0.0.0` would produce an invalid Android `versionCode` of 0.

issues.fix: Re-arm `timer = a.wait(step)` inside `case <-a.logout:` where `step := engine.Step{Outcome: OutcomeLoggedOut, Next: backoff.Steady}`.
issues.problem: On `case <-a.logout:`, `Agent.Run` logs out and reports `Next: backoff.Steady` to `OnStep`, but does not re-arm `timer`. If the previous keepalive timer was about to fire, `TriggerTimer` runs seconds after logout and immediately logs the user back in instead of waiting the steady 5-minute interval.

issues.fix: Determine the subcommand after skipping global flags (`--config <path>` / `--config=<path>`) before deciding whether to install `signal.NotifyContext`.
issues.problem: `strings.HasPrefix(args[0], "-")` installs `signal.NotifyContext` for `os.Interrupt` whenever a global flag like `--config <path>` precedes a subcommand (e.g. `autowifi --config custom.json setup`), causing Ctrl-C at `prompt.Terminal.Ask` to hang on stdin instead of exiting as intended by the comment on lines 46-47.
Troubleshooting tells users to update the `Form` fields in "step 7", but step 7 is the `GET /fgtauth` action; the login POST with the `Form` fields is step 8.
